bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- No business operations and no visibility of resuming any — Following the slump sale of the business to MGM Healthcare Private Limited on February 1, 2024 the Company ceases to have any business operations, and management states there is no visibility of commencing any new business operations in the future. The entity has no revenue-generating activity of its own.
- Going concern rests on the existing cash pile, and the auditor flagged it as an Emphasis of Matter — B S R & Co. LLP drew attention to Note 2(a)(ii) explaining that the Company ceases to have business operations; the standalone financial statements were prepared on a going concern basis only because the Company believes it has sufficient cash and cash equivalent and other bank balances to settle obligations as they fall due, based on the current cash position and projected cash flows. The opinion was not modified, but the going-concern basis depends on a finite, non-replenishing cash balance.
- Corporate restructuring outcome is unresolved and undefined — The Board, with legal advisors and merchant bankers, is still 'evaluating various corporate restructuring options' and only 'progressing with the finalisation of plan'. Neither the option chosen nor a timeline is disclosed, so the terminal value available to shareholders is undetermined.
- Legacy tax litigation carried forward without any operating business to absorb an adverse outcome — The Company continues to contest VAT appeals, a GST appeal and an Income tax appeal; the contingent-liabilities note records sales tax, income tax and GST matters, including the Madras High Court common order of May 28, 2020 on liability to pay VAT under the Tamil Nadu VAT Act, 2006 on stents, valves, x-ray etc. used in treating in-house patients. Management assesses exposure as remote, but any crystallisation would be met purely out of the residual cash.
- Medico-legal claims from the divested hospital business — The MD&A lists 'resolving medico legal cases' among the obligations to be funded going forward, and the contingent-liabilities note records claims against the Company not acknowledged as debts in respect of compensation claims by patients or their relatives. These liabilities were retained by the Company even though the hospital business was transferred.
- No employees and therefore no operating capability or institutional continuity — All employees transferred to MGM Healthcare on the February 1, 2024 divestment, and there was no employee on the payroll of the Company as on March 31, 2026. Any restart or restructuring would have to be built from nothing.
- Concentrated control by the IHH group after completion of the Malar Open Offer — The mandatory open offer by Northern TK Venture Pte Limited, with IHH Healthcare Berhad and Parkway Pantai Limited as PACs, for up to 26% of Malar's paid-up equity completed on November 10, 2025, at a price cut from INR 60.10 to INR 17.60 per share after the INR 42.50 per share dividends. Minority shareholders remaining in a non-operating company are dependent on the controlling group's restructuring decision.
- Ongoing Supreme Court Status Quo Order over the parent-level transaction — The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India passed an order on December 14, 2018 directing that status quo be maintained with regard to the sale of the controlling stake in Fortis Healthcare to IHH Healthcare Berhad, an unresolved overhang at the parent level disclosed in the Board's Report.
